description: A row whose name states a charge is an ion, and the bare element is not where it goes. ecoinvent 3.12's `Rhodium III` and `Palladium II` carry the ions' registry numbers, 16065-89-7 and 16065-88-6; EF 3.1 holds neither number, so the number found nothing and ecoinvent's own bare synonym `Rhodium` reached the element's preferred label, which the label narrowing accepts. Seven rows were published as the metal while AGRIBALYSE's two rows for the same substances minted ion flows, so one substance in air had two published flows and the read-only lookup disagreed with the build (#198). The merge now refuses the bare element for a charge-stated name, and the rows mint the ion. AGRIBALYSE's `Lithium (I)` and `Potassium (I)` are the other half: the names state a charge and the numbers are the elements', the copy-of-EF habit that put vanadium(2+)'s number on `Vanadium (V)`; those numbers are corrected by hand so the rows reach the ions ecoinvent's rows already made. Widening the family to rhodium and palladium also lets the newest-release rule see that ecoinvent renamed six `Palladium` uuids to `Palladium II` and one `Rhodium` uuid to `Rhodium III` between 3.8 and 3.12, so 3.8's rows for those uuids follow 3.12's identity, as `Zinc` follows `Zinc II`. Two more rulings of the same shape follow, both on names that state what the number contradicts: ecoinvent's `Strontium II` and `Caesium I` carry the elements' numbers on every release that states the charge and are corrected to the ions' (the `Molybdenum VI` shape, #181); AGRIBALYSE's six generic `X, Ion` names carry the elements' numbers and lose them, because a generic ion is its own substance that no number names, as ecoinvent's own 3.9.1 deletion says. Five reach the numberless generic ions the list already holds; `Chromium, Ion` mints beside the charged chromium ions.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.12's `Rhodium III` reaches a substance carrying the rhodium(3+) number 16065-89-7
expectations.comment: On the build of 2 September 2026 (b445ff6) this row reached EF 3.1's `Rhodium` in air, registry number 7440-16-6, basis `label`, through ecoinvent's own synonym `Rhodium`. The name states the charge, and the number on the row is the ion's.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.12's six `Palladium II` rows reach one substance, carrying the palladium(2+) number 16065-88-6
expectations.comment: Six compartments, one in air and five in water. All six reached EF's `Palladium`, 7440-05-3, on the build of 2 September 2026.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.8's `Palladium` to surface water, whose uuid 3.12 calls `Palladium II`, reaches the palladium(2+) substance
expectations.comment: The same uuid, 51377cff-…, is `Palladium` under 7440-05-3 in 3.8 and `Palladium II` under 16065-88-6 in 3.12. The element/ion rule (`merge/species.py`) takes the newest release's identity for a uuid, and palladium joined the family on #198, so `ecoinvent-canonical-identities.json`, regenerated by its tool, now records the six water and air uuids. On the build of 2 September 2026 the 3.8 row reached bare `Palladium`. Selected by uuid: the newest release's name is what the build records the 3.8 row under, so `Palladium` is no longer findable for it. One of the six, to surface water; the six share the rule.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's `Rhodium (III)` reaches the rhodium(3+) substance by its number rather than minting a second one
expectations.comment: ecoinvent merges first and now mints the ion; AGRIBALYSE's row, carrying the same number, finds it. On the build of 2 September 2026 the row's outcome was `created`.

expectations.title: One substance carries the rhodium(3+) number, and it is called Rhodium(3+)
expectations.comment: Held so that ecoinvent's mint and AGRIBALYSE's row cannot drift into two substances again. Already true on the build of 2 September 2026, where the one substance was AGRIBALYSE's mint; the row claims above are what changes. The label is this list's spelling of a stated charge, written by a curated name in `flow-object-overrides.json` the way the minted generic ions' were (#141); on the branch build of 2 September 2026 before that row the mint published as `Rhodium III`.

expectations.title: One substance carries the palladium(2+) number 16065-88-6, and it is called Palladium(2+)
AGRIBALYSE's six `Lithium (I)` rows reach `Lithium(1+)` by number
expectations.comment: AGRIBALYSE ships the name with the element's number 7439-93-2, and on the build of 2 September 2026 the six rows reached bare `Lithium`. `agribalyse-3.2-manual-fixes.json` replaces the number with the ion's, 17341-24-1, the number ecoinvent's `Lithium I` rows carry to the same substance.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's twelve `Potassium (I)` rows reach `Potassium(1+)` by number
expectations.comment: Shipped with the element's 7440-09-7; the twelve rows reached bare `Potassium` on the build of 2 September 2026. Corrected to 24203-36-9, the number on ecoinvent's `Potassium I` rows. Selected by the corrected number rather than the vendor's spelling: once the rows reach the substance the build records them under its name, `Potassium(1+)`, and the spelling `Potassium (I)` is no longer findable, the shape #190's palladium claim already notes.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.12's thirteen `Strontium II` rows reach `Strontium(2+)` by the corrected number
expectations.comment: Shipped under the element's 7440-24-6; on the build of 2 September 2026 the thirteen reached bare `Strontium`, beside AGRIBALYSE's twelve `Strontium(2+)` rows on the ion. Selected by the corrected number, which is what the build records once the fix has run.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.8's thirteen `Strontium II` rows reach `Strontium(2+)` too
expectations.comment: The same uuids, corrected in 3.8's own fix file.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.12's five `Caesium I` rows reach `Cesium(1+)` by the corrected number
expectations.comment: Shipped under the element's 7440-46-2; on the build of 2 September 2026 the five reached bare `Cesium`, beside AGRIBALYSE's three `Cesium (I)` rows on the ion.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.8's five `Caesium I` rows reach `Cesium(1+)` too
expectations.comment: The same uuids, corrected in 3.8's own fix file.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's `Antimony, Ion` rows reach the numberless `Antimony, Ion` by name once the element's number is off
expectations.comment: The worked example of the five that reach a generic ion the list already holds; copper, iron, tin and titanium have the same shape and are held below by count. On the build of 2 September 2026 the eleven reached bare `Antimony` on 7440-36-0.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's fifteen `Copper, Ion` rows reach `Copper, Ion`
AGRIBALYSE's twelve `Iron, Ion` rows reach `Iron, Ion`
AGRIBALYSE's twelve `Tin, Ion` rows reach `Tin, Ion`
AGRIBALYSE's twelve `Titanium, Ion` rows reach EF 3.1's `Titanium, ion`
expectations.comment: EF's own generic titanium ion, which carries 22541-75-9 (#143); the name reaches it as ecoinvent's `Titanium ion` rows do.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's thirteen `Chromium, Ion` rows mint one substance, `Chromium, Ion`, and all reach it
expectations.comment: No list publishes a generic chromium ion, so with the element's number off the rows mint one beside `Chromium(3+)` and `Chromium(6+)`. On the build of 2 September 2026 the thirteen reached bare `Chromium` on 7440-47-3.

expectations.title: The minted `Chromium, Ion` is typed a monoatomic ion of chromium and carries no registry number, like its five siblings
expectations.comment: What the enrichment gives a charge-less ion: the type, the `ion_of` relationship to chromium and the element, and nothing more, because Common Chemistry and PubChem hold no record for an ion of unstated charge. `Antimony, Ion`, `Copper, Ion`, `Iron, Ion` and `Tin, Ion` carry exactly that (#141); a number or a charge would be the reinterpretation plan §3a refuses.
